title: Cognitive Tele-Palpation: Context-Based Haptic Event Detection
abstract: Performing clinical palpation in telemedicine remains a critical challenge due to the limitations of current approaches. Autonomous robotic examinations lack the adaptability required for dynamic contact conditions, while direct bilateral teleoperation is fundamentally constrained by the stability-transparency trade-off and communication delays. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes Cognitive Tele-Palpation, a clinician-in-the-loop framework that infers semantic haptic events (Normal, Edge, and Tumor) purely from remote-side interaction signals. Rather than relying solely on delay-sensitive raw force transmission, the proposed framework integrates these inferred events into a real-time cumulative probabilistic map. By providing this intuitive semantic feedback, the system enables remote operators to confidently localize abnormalities even under attenuated haptic transparency. The underlying detection model employs a three-step training strategy, incorporating context-aware backbone pre-training, latent space clustering, and domain calibration, to generalize across unseen environments. Experimental evaluations on a bilateral teleoperation platform demonstrate a classification accuracy exceeding 95% on test data. Furthermore, during real-time experiments on unseen heterogeneous phantoms, the framework achieved reliable tumor localization with an area-precision exceeding 90%. Compared to an autonomous scanning baseline, the human-in-the-loop approach demonstrated significantly enhanced domain alignment in the latent space. Ultimately, these findings indicate that context-based event inference and multi-contact evidence integration effectively reduce diagnostic uncertainty, establishing a fundamental prerequisite toward haptic event-based local feedback.

title: A Physics-Based Closed-Loop Robotic Bioprinting Framework towards Volumetric Muscle Loss Treatment
abstract: Robotic bioprinting and Direct Ink Writing (DIW) are being explored towards the treatment of Volumetric Muscle Loss (VML). While previous studies have shown the importance of proper parameter selection on the print outcome, existing approaches often rely on time- and material-intensive design of experiments methods, or require large, well-curated datasets for training machine learning models. In this paper, we propose a physics-based closed-loop robotic bioprinting system capable of near real-time parameter adaptation. The system integrates a 3D point cloud camera and fully autonomous vision-based algorithms to provide quantitative evaluation of printed constructs. This evaluation is fed into a controller that adjusts printing parameters to achieve a desired bead thickness. To assess the framework’s performance, four experimental configurations were tested, each repeated three times. In these tests, printing began from an arbitrary initial parameter value, and the controller was tasked with adjusting the parameters to reach the desired thickness. The system converged in all trials, achieving a tracking error below 0.5 mm within an average of 5.2 seconds from the start of printing. The low standard deviation of the converged pressure over different tests (0.04 bar on average) demonstrates robustness and repeatability. Additional experiments were conducted with the controller turned off, enabling direct comparison with open-loop DIW bioprinting, further confirming the effectiveness of the proposed closed-loop framework in achieving the desired bead geometry.

title: Motion Planning with Model-Based Diffusion Via Constraint Optimization and Adaptive Scheduling
abstract: Single-Robot Motion Planning (SRMP) in highly non-convex constrained environments, where robots must satisfy collision-free guarantees, dynamic feasibility, and task-related constraints, is challenging under complex constraints and computational limits. Recent Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) approaches recast the SRMP as trajectory optimization that samples from a posterior over trajectories, using known dynamics, and analytically estimates the score function from rollout samples to guide diffusion denoising toward a low-cost, clean trajectory without demonstration learning. While existing works further adapt MBD to constrained environments and showcase promising performance, they are still limited by (1) enforcing safety either via soft feasibility diffusion priors or hard projection operators, but lack a unified framework to integrate both, and (2) fixing safety enforcement to neglect the changing of diffusion scheduling. Therefore, we introduce Model-Based Diffusion via Constraint Optimization and Adaptive Scheduling (MD-COAS) for SRMP that unifies the inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method (iALM) soft diffusion prior with a Convex Feasible Set (CFS)-based hard projection operator, and adaptively schedules and co-optimizes safety enforcement, along with diffusion scheduling. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves higher safety & success rates, faster convergence, and lower final costs than baseline planners on randomly generated highly non-convex 2D benchmarks and a 7-DoF robot arm avoidance task.

title: How Are Cells Lately? Persistent Monitoring of the Honeybee Comb under Stochastic Observability
abstract: Honeybees are essential pollinators, and their long-term decline threatens ecosystem stability. The need for scalable colony health monitoring has driven a shift from manual inspections of honeycomb contents toward automated approaches, including robotic mapping of the honeycomb. Mapping is usually opportunistic, as systems must balance scanning with other sensing tasks, resulting in a limited sensing budget. Moreover, the honeycomb is commonly occluded by bees, making the observability of individual cells inherently stochastic. In our mapping systems, we aim to minimize the time since the last observation for all cells in the map. This work frames comb mapping as a persistent monitoring problem and evaluates strategies combining spatial planning and pre-allocation of capture duration. To enable intelligent decision-making, we formulate a short-horizon spatio-temporal Poisson count model that estimates the expected number of observed cells for set locations as a function of capture time. Using data collected in the last season, we show that an adaptive method balancing short-term exploitation with long-term coverage fairness outperforms the current system strategy. The framework is, by design, also ready to support active learning and long-term adaptation to evolving colony dynamics.

title: TactileReflex: Noise-Statistics-Driven Vision-Tactile Reflex Control for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
abstract: Manipulating fragile deformable containers, such as disposable plastic cups filled with liquid, demands real-time grip-force adaptation within an extremely narrow force margin: insufficient force causes slip, while excessive force irreversibly deforms the thin wall. Existing approaches struggle to achieve such force-sensitive manipulation tasks. We propose a noise-statistics-based calibration-driven reflex control paradigm with vision-based tactile sensing: by analyzing the sensor's intrinsic noise characteristics (via a brief static-hold-and-unload protocol), we directly derive all controller thresholds, eliminating external force calibration, trial-and-error manual tuning, or material-specific physical models. Instantiating this paradigm, we present TactileReflex, a three-channel closed-loop controller that extracts three image-level proxies, shear intensity (Sy), contact intensity (Fn), and center of pressure (C), from dual visuo-tactile sensors and drives prioritized reflex channels at ∼12 Hz for slip suppression, weight-adaptive release, and force protection. Each channel closes the loop directly on its proxy via noise-derived thresholds. Ablation demonstrates that only the full three-channel system is able to prevent irreversible container deformation (5/5 success vs. at most 1/5 for partial configurations). In a dynamic pouring task, fixed-effort baselines fail in all 10 attempts due to pose drift, while TactileReflex achieves 9/10 success across two water volumes. As a self-contained and interpretable controller, TactileReflex can serve as a plug-and-play safety layer beneath high-level manipulation pipelines, including haptic-free VR teleoperation and vision-language-action (VLA) policies.

title: Navigating the Proximity-Safety Balance: Constraint Decomposition for Human Following in Pedestrian Crowds
abstract: Following a target human in crowded environments involves an inherent conflict between staying close to the target and navigating safely among surrounding pedestrians and obstacles. This conflict becomes more severe in dense scenarios, where aggressive following risks collisions and conservative margins lead to target loss, especially when pedestrian behaviors are unfamiliar or unpredictable. Existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods typically encode these competing objectives into a single dense reward, but the resulting proximity-safety balance is implicit and difficult to adjust across conditions. To address this, we decompose the human-following task into a sparse task reward and independent cost constraints within a multi-constraint RL formulation, where each constraint is managed through cost thresholds with direct behavioral meaning rather than implicit reward weight ratios, allowing explicit and tunable control over the trade-off. We further quantify the prediction uncertainty of human motions and integrate these estimates into the RL costs to enhance safety under unpredictable conditions. Extensive experiments across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings demonstrate that our method achieves an effective proximity-safety balance compared to baselines. Real-robot deployment further validates the feasibility of our method in real-world scenarios. More details are available on our project page: https://nav-ps-balance.github.io/.

title: Proprioceptive Shape Sensing for Tendon-Driven Multi-Segment Continuum Robotic Bronchoscope
abstract: Accurate proprioceptive shape sensing is critical for the safety and efficacy of robot-assisted bronchoscopy. Traditional analytical models struggle with nonlinear tendon hysteresis and environmental contact forces, while pure data-driven approaches lack physical grounding and geometric constraints. This paper proposes a physics-embedded graph state space model that formulates continuum robot shape reconstruction as a two-point boundary value problem on the Special Euclidean group. The framework introduces a viscoelasticity-informed state space model to explicitly capture temporal tendon relaxation dynamics. To resolve spatial deformations,a bidirectional graph neural network learns to fuse proximal motor actuation with sparse distal electromagnetic sensor data under geometric boundary constraints. Extensive experiments on a dual-segment continuum bronchoscope validate the approach. In free-space evaluations, the framework successfully decouples complex multi-segment motions, achieving a root mean square error of 1.1 millimeters. During dynamic navigation within a constrained bronchial phantom, the model exhibits exceptional robustness to unmodeled tissue contact forces, maintaining reconstruction errors strictly below the 2.0 millimeter clinical safety threshold. By eliminating the reliance on distal force sensors, this method provides highly reliable shape estimation essential for active constraint control and safe endobronchial navigation.

title: SenseExpo: Spatial Exploration and Navigation Via Scene Estimation from Expeditious Predictive Operators
abstract: We present SenseExpo, a lightweight framework that substantially improves autonomous exploration efficiency by integrating a compact map prediction network into a frontier-based exploration strategy. SenseExpo addresses two long-standing challenges in classical methods—high computa- tional overhead and poor environmental generalization. Our prediction network combines Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Transformers, and Fast Fourier Convolution (FFC) to achieve a remarkably small footprint of only 709K parameters. Despite its compactness, SenseExpo outperforms U-Net (24.5M) and LaMa (51M) on the KTH dataset, achieving PSNR 9.026 and SSIM 0.718, representing a 38.7% PSNR gain over LaMa. Cross-domain evaluation further verifies strong generalization with an FID of 161.55 on HouseExpo, surpassing comparable models. In exploration experiments, SenseExpo reduces explo- ration time by 67.9% on KTH and 77.1% on MRPB 1.0 relative to MapEx. Implemented as a plug-and-play ROS (Robot Oper- ating System) node, our framework integrates seamlessly with existing navigation stacks, providing an efficient, deployable solution for resource-constrained robotic systems.

title: HI-MAPF - Towards Resource-Efficient Multi-Agent Deployment
abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is central to coordinating multiple agents in shared or contested environments. Existing algorithmic solutions to MAPF impose significant requirements on communication, sensing, and computation, limiting their applicability in resource-constrained robotic deployments. For instance, centralized search methods require access to global state information and high-bandwidth channels, while distributed learning-based methods depend on sophisticated onboard perception (e.g., LiDAR, RGB-D cameras) and frequent inter-agent communication. Consequently, these methods incur high hardware, computational, and communication costs that form a critical bottleneck for long-term robotic deployment. To address these limitations, we formulate information-centric MAPF (I-MAPF) and introduce HI-MAPF, a hybrid framework that augments decentralized planning with a lightweight centralized coordinator. We further introduce a method-agnostic metric, Information Units (IU), to quantify coordination overhead as a proxy for deployment cost. We evaluate HI--MAPF against recent communication-focused algorithms in both simulation, across unstructured and structured environments with 8 to 128 agents, and on ground robots in a physical deployment, demonstrating 2x to 510x reduction in information sharing while maintaining high success rates. Our results show that in controlled environments, HI-MAPF eliminates the need for sophisticated onboard perception, expensive compute, and frequent inter-agent communication, enabling coordination through minimal event-triggered alerts.

title: Beyond Shallow-Water Photorealism: Physically and Sensor-Grounded Simulation for Deep-Sea Robotics
abstract: Many recent underwater simulators emphasize vi- sual realism at the expense of physical fidelity, focusing on shallow-water effects with limited relevance in deep-water envi- ronments and high computational cost. In this work, we shift the focus toward deep-sea physical and sensor realism. We present a physics- and sensor-grounded extension of the Stonefish simulator that augments its hydrodynamic models with stochastic IMU and DVL drift, magnetometer disturbances, higher-order hydrody- namics, terramechanics, pressure-driven environmental variabil- ity, and physically based underwater optics. These additions are designed to better capture the forces and measurements shaping the behavior of deep-ocean AUVs, ROVs, landers, ASVs, and gliders, while remaining compatible with real-time simulation. This work advances underwater simulation toward more repre- sentative deep-sea operating conditions, which is particularly rel- evant for long-duration navigation and learning-based autonomy, where inaccurate sensor and environmental models introduce non-physical artifacts and overly optimistic performance. While challenges remain, including complex fluid–structure interactions and full environmental stochasticity, the proposed framework provides a practical foundation for navigation, perception, and autonomy research under deep-sea conditions.

title: Enabling Scalable Infrastructure-To-Vehicle Data Generation: A High-Fidelity Fusion Pipeline with a Scene Harmonizer for Visual and Logical Consistency
abstract: Data-driven autonomous driving demands massive, diverse, and precise datasets. While real-world collection is cost-prohibitive and game-engine simulations suffer from sim-to-real gaps, emerging generative world models, though photorealistic, often struggle with temporal inconsistencies and geometric distortions due to a scarcity of high-fidelity 4D training data. Infrastructure-to-Vehicle systems offer a scalable alternative by capturing real-world traffic behaviors; however, current approaches relying on sparse views fail to render high-quality novel views from the vehicle perspective. To address these challenges, we propose a high-fidelity fusion pipeline for scalable I2V data generation by amortizing one-time static reconstruction across many real traffic sequences, target viewpoints, and environmental conditions. Our key strategy is to pre-reconstruct a high-quality static scene from dense scans and merge it with dynamic objects reconstructed from real-time observations. While this ensures physical fidelity, it introduces a critical dual-inconsistency challenge: the static scene's fixed appearance and logic clash with dynamic objects captured under varied conditions. To resolve this, we introduce SceneHarmonizer, a lightweight framework that efficiently repaints the static 3D scene to match any target illumination and dynamically controls semantic elements like traffic lights. This ensures the generated data achieves both visual and logical consistency. We validate our framework on downstream perception models, demonstrating that our synthetic data possesses a feature distribution nearly identical to real-world data. Crucially, our pipeline provides the physically grounded 4D priors essential for reliable simulation, bridging the gap for both perception training and future world model development.

title: REST: Receding Horizon Explorative Steiner Tree for Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation
abstract: Zero-shot Object-goal Navigation (ZSON) requires navigating unknown environments to find a target object without task-specific training. Prior hierarchical training-free solutions invest in scene understanding (belief) and high-level decision-making (policy), yet overlook the design of option, i.e., a subgoal candidate proposed from evolving belief and presented to policy for selection. In practice, options are reduced into a flat set of isolated waypoints: single points hide the value gathered along the journey; an unstructured collection obscures the relationships among candidates. Our insight is that the option space should be a tree of paths. Full paths expose en-route information gain that destination-only scoring systematically neglects; a forking tree of shared prefixes enables coarse-to-fine LLM reasoning that dismisses or pursues entire branches before examining individual leaves, compressing the combinatorial path space into an efficient hierarchy. We instantiate this insight in REST (Receding-Horizon Explorative Steiner Tree), a training-free framework that (1) grows an agent-centric tree of collision-free, informative paths as the option space via sampling-based planning; (2) builds an open-vocabulary 3D semantic map from online RGB-D streams; and (3) textualizes each branch into a spatial narrative and selects the next-best path through chain-of-thought LLM reasoning. REST achieves competitive or state-of-the-art success rate and path efficiency across the Gibson, HM3D, and HSSD benchmarks.

title: Multi-Sensor Fusion-based Situational Awareness for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships: Current Progress and Future Work
abstract: With advances in probabilistic inference, AI, and high-performance computing, autonomous navigation has made great strides. Yet, ships remain uniquely challenged by dynamic ocean environments and long offshore operations. These conditions place high demands on maritime situational awareness systems, which must ensure robust object detection and tracking while remaining cost-effective. This paper presents a multi-object tracking system specifically designed for autonomous ships, grounded in a deep understanding of their distinctive operational characteristics. The proposed architecture integrates multiple detection and navigation sensors with an AI-based perception algorithm and a probabilistic data fusion framework. With modularity and scalability at its core, the system processes sensor data through two specialized stages to ensure optimal performance. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through real-world trials under realistic maritime conditions. Beyond system performance, this study highlights the limitations of relying solely on local awareness systems in commercial maritime operations. It underscores the necessity for a standardized, systematic approach to generating and sharing positional data among vessels—via Next-Generation AIS and inter-ship communication. Drawing inspiration from structured environments in robotics, we suggest that such an approach offers a practical path to balancing operational safety with economic viability. Ultimately, this strategy may accelerate the adoption of autonomous vessels amid the complexities of modern maritime practice.

title: Dataset Development and Preliminary Study for Semantic 3D Skeleton Extraction in Precision Agricultural Robotics
abstract: A seasonal real tree dataset was constructed in a pear orchard environment using RGB-D cameras and LiDAR sensors under leaf-off conditions. The acquired 3D data provides detailed representations of trunk and branch structures in realistic orchard environments. RGB-D and LiDAR point clouds are integrated to generate dense tree representations, followed by ground removal and DBSCAN clustering for individual tree segmentation. ADTree-based modeling is then applied to each segmented tree to generate corresponding skeleton ground truths. The constructed ground truth represents the hierarchical branch topology of each tree and provides a basis for evaluating tree skeleton reconstruction methods. Additional data collection under leaf-on conditions is planned to investigate structural variations caused by foliage changes and enable seasonal comparison. The proposed dataset will be utilized for training and evaluation of a Flow Matching-based generative framework for tree skeletonization, supporting the analysis of skeleton reconstruction performance under realistic orchard conditions.

title: One-Shot Grasp Adaptation for Tightly Packed Scenes via Prior-Guided Recovery of Affordance Regions
abstract: Robotic grasping in tightly packed scenes remains challenging due to the limited availability of grasp affordance regions. Existing vision-based recognition and grasp detection methods often struggle to generalize across domains and require scene-specific data for reliable adaptation, resulting in substantial annotation effort and computational cost. To address these limitations, we propose a one-shot adaptation framework for grasp detection in tightly packed scenes. The framework requires only a single RGB-D observation and autonomously generates training data without manual annotation. A prior-guided affordance recovery method is introduced to identify undetected or misdetected graspable regions, followed by primitive fitting for robust grasp planning and label generation. The generated labels are further augmented through simulated object translations, while an optimized loss function enables efficient fine-tuning of an existing grasp detection model. Real-world experiments demonstrate effective adaptation across varying object numbers, randomized arrangements, and novel instances in tightly packed scenarios.

title: Betting for Sim-to-Real Performance Testing
abstract: Roboticists are, in some sense, gamblers: every sim-to-real deployment is a wager that simulation-implied performance will carry over to real-world hardware. This paper formalizes that wager for sim-to-real performance testing (i.e., given a fixed policy, controller, or robotic system, whether model-based, learning-based, or hybrid, as it stands, one seeks to test its performance under a certain real-world environment for validation, regulation compliance, and other purposes). Specifically, we bring scaled simulators to facilitate real-world robot performance inference and certificate through the perspective of ``betting''. This allows practically efficient (i.e. with few real-world tests) and provably accurate (i.e. close to ground truth measure) performance tests of various robotic systems. Within the inference tasks, the sim-to-real bet induces a bet-weighted estimator that provably outperforms Monte Carlo and composes with importance sampling for rare events. Within the certificate tasks, the same bet accumulates an e-process, and the candidates it never rules out form an anytime-valid certificate, valid whether or not the bank of simulators is any good. Extended experiments are performed across a variety of applications including synthetic examples, robotic manipulation, locomotion, and navigation tasks.

title: Intelligent Mobile Robot with Person Following and Fall Detection
abstract: This paper presents a compact indoor assistive-robot architecture that couples person following, skeleton-based fall detection, and map-aware navigation. A wheeled platform carries RGB and depth cameras: RGB frames drive detection, tracking, pose estimation, and spatio-temporal action recognition, while depth provides metric target range and supports RGB-D simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). The perception prototype uses the PP-Human pipeline with HRNet keypoints and an ST-GCN classifier. On a six-clip proof-of-concept subset of the UR Fall Detection dataset, all three fall clips triggered an alert and none of the three normal clips produced a false alert; the mean first-alert time was 5.07~s from clip start. These results validate integration feasibility rather than population-level accuracy. The proposed navigation layer converts the tracked person's depth into a map-frame goal and plans around static furniture while maintaining a reasonable following distance.

title: Who Creates Agricultural Robots? Place-Conscious Pilots to Scale Community Participation in Robotics & AI R&D&D
abstract: Robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and automation are transforming agriculture, yet a critical gap remains between the communities these technologies are intended to serve and the Research, Development, and Deployment (R&D&D) processes that shape them. Although rural communities comprise approximately 41% of the global population and possess substantial agricultural knowledge, they are often positioned as technology adopters rather than contributors to innovation. This study explores how place-conscious pathways can expand participation in agricultural robotics and AI R&D&D by engaging rural communities as contributors, co-creators, and future technology leaders. Building on a multi-year collaboration with rural Pennsylvania communities beginning in 2019, these are two pilot initiatives. The first, the FIRA Robotics Village, connected agricultural robotics companies, researchers, growers, students, and community members around technologies tailored to regional crops and farming systems. The second, PA Robotics & AI Scholars, created customized pathways within Carnegie Mellon University's Robotics Institute Summer Scholars (RISS) program for students from agricultural and rural backgrounds to participate in robotics and AI research. Results suggest that place-conscious engagement can shift participation beyond technology exposure toward meaningful contribution. The FIRA Robotics Village provided opportunities for community members and students to connect with innovators, encounter emerging technologies, and envision themselves as participants in agricultural innovation. PA Robotics & AI Scholars demonstrated how rural and agricultural students contribute valuable perspectives shaped by farming, rural life, and community experience. Across both pilots, participants contributed contextual knowledge, observations, and questions that may otherwise be absent from technology development processes. Together, the pilots suggest a progression from Explore → Participate → Grow → Contribute → Lead, representing a shift from workforce preparation toward capability creation, where communities gain the ability to interpret, shape, and influence technological change rather than simply respond to it. The findings indicate that rural communities are not only locations where agricultural robotics and AI will be deployed, but also sources of knowledge, innovation, future researchers, and future technology leaders. Future work will expand these pilots across additional agricultural contexts to examine how place-conscious pathways can be adapted to diverse communities and production systems while investigating long-term participant outcomes and mechanisms for integrating rural knowledge into robotics and AI R&D&D. Pennsylvania serves as an initial demonstration environment, with the broader goal of developing a framework for connecting community assets, local expertise, and agricultural innovation ecosystems.

title: Geometric Sparse Depth Estimation as a Prior for Robot Navigation
abstract: Reliable 3D spatial understanding is essential for autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, and 3D scene reconstruction. Although state-of-the-art depth completion techniques achieve high accuracy, they often depend on heavy foundation models or require explicit sparse 3D measurements. This paper presents a novel, geometrically derived depth estimation method using epipolar transfer with only two monocular images and camera pose estimates. By leveraging known camera motion, the proposed approach synthesizes a virtual stereo pair through epipolar transfer, transforming the two-view temporal correspondence problem into a standard stereo triangulation task while mitigating common geometric degeneracies. The end-to-end pipeline incorporates feature matching, epipolar line computation, virtual frame synthesis, and disparity estimation. We evaluate and validate our method across diverse environments, including outdoor flights with a DJI Mavic Air 2 drone and indoor cluttered scenes within an OptiTrack motion capture facility. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves nearly 90% depth accuracy while maintaining low computational overhead.
